identity.title: Estimating the Temperature and Density of a Spicule from 100 GHz Data Obtained with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We succeeded in observing two large spicules simultaneously with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), and the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA)

targets.name: 100GHz spicule and MgII/304A spicule (solar limb, 26 April 2017)

coordinates.value: not stated (limb near X=956'' in Mg II)

evidence.loc: 3 The spicules observed with ALMA, IRIS, and AIA/SDO
evidence.quote: In the Mg II image, the solar limb is located around X=956$''$

question.value: What are the temperature and density of a spicule seen at 100 GHz with ALMA, and how does it relate to spicules seen in IRIS Mg II and AIA 304 A?

evidence.quote: To obtain the physical parameters of the 100GHz spicule, we estimate the optical depths as a function of temperature and density using two different methods.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2016.1.00070.S.
We used the Band3 receiver and the Time Division Mode (TDM) of the correlator.
a synthesized image shows a distribution of intensity at 100 GHz with a bandwidth of about 8 GHz.
The sizes of the synthesized beam are 2$''$.67 and 1$''$.88 along the major and minor axes, respectively.

evidence.loc: 3 The spicules observed with ALMA, IRIS, and AIA/SDO
evidence.quote: This signal level is much larger than the noise, i.e. $\sim$2.6 K (Shimojo et al. 2017b).
our observation was carried out between 14:22 – 16:13UT on 26 April 2017.

provided.value: Mg II 2796 slit-jaw images, 40 s cadence, 0.4'' resolution

evidence.quote: IRIS obtained slit-jaw images of Mg II (2796Å) bands with a cadence and a spatial resolution of 40 s and 0$''$.40, respectively.

provided.value: 304 A and 193 A context images, 12 s cadence, 1.5'' resolution

evidence.quote: We also use 304Å (He II) and 193Å (Fe XII) band images taken with AIA. They provide context filtergrams with a cadence of 12 s.

method.value: Per-2 s images with CLEAN after phase-only self-calibration; jitter removed by shifting images using auto-correlation offsets

evidence.quote: To remove jitter motion caused by the remaining phase error, we spatially shift the images based on the offsets estimated by the auto-correlation of the images.

method.value: Subtract pre-event brightness from event brightness pixel by pixel; correct by filling factor 0.25 (assumed width 0.5'' vs apparent 2'')

evidence.loc: 3 The spicules observed with ALMA, IRIS, and AIA/SDO
evidence.quote: Thus, we use 960 K (= 240 K/0.25) as the brightness temperature of the 100GHz spicule.

evidence.loc: 3 The spicules observed with ALMA, IRIS, and AIA/SDO
evidence.quote: we assume that the width of the 100GHz spicule is 0$''$.5

analysis_steps.goal: Optical depth vs temperature, observed and modeled

method.value: Observed tau = -ln(1-Tb/T); model free-free optical depth for assumed T and density with 0.5'' line-of-sight depth; intersection gives T and n

evidence.loc: 3 The spicules observed with ALMA, IRIS, and AIA/SDO
evidence.quote: The black line estimates from the observations and the colored line of the model cross when we assume the kinetic temperature of the plasma and the number density of ionized hydrogens

findings_qualitative.value: 100GHz spicule is a macrospicule without a hot sheath

evidence.quote: These results suggest that the 100GHz spicule presented in this paper is classified to a macrospicule without a hot sheath in former terminology.

claims.hypothesis: Are the 100GHz spicule and the MgII/304A spicule physically related?
claims.experiment: Compared ALMA, IRIS and AIA images and velocities over time
claims.result: Overlap only early; different velocities (~40 vs ~70 km/s); no counterpart afterward
claims.finding: They are individual events with no physical relationship

evidence.quote: It suggests that the spicules are individual events and do not have a physical relationship.

claims.hypothesis: What are the temperature and density of the 100GHz spicule?
claims.experiment: Compared observed and modeled free-free optical depth
claims.finding: Values consistent with the 193 A absorbing structure

evidence.quote: The estimated values can explain the absorbing structure in the 193Å image

why_this_method.value: Millimeter emission satisfies LTE, making parameters easier to derive than from chromospheric lines

evidence.quote: Since the millimeter waves emitted from the chromospheric plasma satisfies the LTE condition, it is relatively easier than other chromospheric lines to derive the physical parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: Width comparable to beam, so the actual width may be narrower

evidence.loc: 3 The spicules observed with ALMA, IRIS, and AIA/SDO

limitations_admitted.value: Only relative brightness temperatures because single-dish data not combined
